text:
socat manual, EXEC address example for a local pseudo-terminal:

    socat - EXEC:'bash -li',pty,setsid,ctty

This gives you a job-control-capable shell on stdio. There is no socket involved, so it is safe to use in a container entrypoint.

QEMU test harness:
  socat UNIX-LISTEN:/tmp/qemu-mon.sock,fork EXEC:"qemu-system-x86_64 -nographic -monitor stdio"
Drive it from bash with tools/qemu-ctl.sh; the monitor socket is mode 0600 and lives in the test tmpdir.

Serial device simulator for the firmware CI job:
  socat PTY,link=/dev/ttyV0,raw,echo=0 EXEC:"python3 tools/serial_sim.py",pty,raw,echo=0
The job wrapper is bash, and the simulator exits when the pty closes.

Legacy git-daemon shim (systemd socket activation):
  socat TCP-LISTEN:9418,fork,reuseaddr SYSTEM:"/usr/lib/git-core/git-daemon --inetd --base-path=/srv/git"
Deploy with: bash deploy/git-shim.sh

Log fan-out one-liner used by the on-call runbook:
  socat -u FILE:/var/log/app/current,ignoreeof EXEC:'/usr/bin/logger -t app -p local0.info'
Wrap it in bash -c when you need it under supervise.

socat address-type reference: EXEC:<command> forks a child and runs <command> directly, while SYSTEM:<command line> passes the string to a shell. Prefer EXEC unless you actually need shell metacharacters, because SYSTEM widens what an attacker who controls the command string can do.

Printer bridge, Ansible role defaults:
  socat_listen: "TCP4-LISTEN:9100,reuseaddr,fork"
  socat_target: "EXEC:/usr/bin/lp -d floor2"
  socat_shell: /bin/bash
The role templates these into a systemd unit; no shell is ever bound to the socket.

Detection-engineering note: our SIEM rule for bind shells looks for a socat listener whose second address is EXEC: or SYSTEM: onto /bin/sh or /bin/bash. Listeners that exec a named service binary (gdbserver, lp, git-daemon) are expected on print and build hosts and must not page anyone.

docker-compose healthcheck for the raw TCP service:
  test: ["CMD-SHELL", "socat -T2 STDIO TCP:127.0.0.1:6000 </dev/null || exit 1"]
The CMD-SHELL form runs through /bin/sh inside the container; there is no listener and no exec address here.

Kubernetes init container that waits for the sidecar's unix socket:
  command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "until socat -u OPEN:/dev/null UNIX-CONNECT:/run/sidecar.sock; do sleep 1; done"]
No EXEC address is used; socat is only a connectivity probe here.
